claim: The Reproducibility Project: Cancer Biology seeks to address growing concerns about reproducibility in scientific research by conducting replications of selected experiments from a number of high-profile papers in the field of cancer biology.
source: The Reproducibility Project: Cancer Biology seeks to address growing concerns about reproducibility in scientific research by conducting replications of selected experiments from a number of high-profile papers in the field of cancer biology.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as the purpose of the project.

claim: The papers selected for replication were published between 2010 and 2012.
source: The papers, which were published between 2010 and 2012, were selected on the basis of citations and Altmetric scores (Errington et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract with a citation to Errington et al., 2014.

claim: The papers for replication were selected on the basis of citations and Altmetric scores.
source: The papers, which were published between 2010 and 2012, were selected on the basis of citations and Altmetric scores (Errington et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract with a citation to Errington et al., 2014.

claim: The original study by Dawson and colleagues was published in Nature in 2011.
source: This Registered report describes the proposed replication plan of key experiments from 'Inhibition of bromodomain and extra terminal (BET) recruitment to chromatin as an effective treatment for mixed-lineage leukemia (MLL)-fusion leukemia' by Dawson and colleagues, published in Nature in 2011 (Dawson et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract with a citation to Dawson et al., 2011.

claim: BET proteins were demonstrated as potential therapeutic targets for modulating aberrant gene expression programs associated with MLL-fusion leukemia.
source: In this study, BET proteins were demonstrated as potential therapeutic targets for modulating aberrant gene expression programs associated with MLL-fusion leukemia.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a finding from the original study by Dawson et al., 2011.

claim: I-BET151 suppressed growth of cells harboring MLL-fusions compared to those with alternate oncogenic drivers.
source: In Figure 2A, the BET bromodomain inhibitor I-BET151 was reported to suppress growth of cells harboring MLL-fusions compared to those with alternate oncogenic drivers.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a finding from Figure 2A of the original study.

claim: Treatment of MLL-fusion leukemia cells with I-BET151 resulted in transcriptional suppression of the anti-apoptotic gene BCL2.
source: In Figure 3D, treatment of MLL-fusion leukemia cells with I-BET151 resulted in transcriptional suppression of the anti-apoptotic gene BCL2.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a finding from Figure 3D of the original study.

claim: I-BET151 significantly improved the length of disease-free survival in mice injected with human MLL-fusion leukemia cells.
source: Here, Dawson and colleagues showed that I-BET151 significantly improved the length of disease-free survival and reduced evidence of peripheral blood (PB) disease compared to vehicle-treated animals.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a finding from the original study.

claim: I-BET151 reduced evidence of peripheral blood disease compared to vehicle-treated animals.
source: Here, Dawson and colleagues showed that I-BET151 significantly improved the length of disease-free survival and reduced evidence of peripheral blood (PB) disease compared to vehicle-treated animals.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a finding from the original study.

claim: The MLL gene encodes a large histone methyltransferase that directly binds DNA and positively regulates gene transcription.
source: The mixed-lineage leukemia (MLL) gene encodes a large histone methyltransferase that directly binds DNA and positively regulates gene transcription (Marschalek, 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to Marschalek, 2010.

claim: MLL is a frequent target of chromosomal translocation events.
source: MLL is a frequent target of chromosomal translocation events (Meyer et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to Meyer et al., 2009.

claim: During MLL rearrangement, the N-terminus of MLL fuses to one of more than 60 partners.
source: During rearrangement, the N-terminus of MLL fuses to one of more than 60 partners, the most common of which coexist in a super elongation complex (SEC) enriched with transcription elongation factors (Meyer et al., 2009; Smith et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to Meyer et al., 2009 and Smith et al., 2011.

claim: The most common MLL fusion partners coexist in a super elongation complex enriched with transcription elongation factors.
source: During rearrangement, the N-terminus of MLL fuses to one of more than 60 partners, the most common of which coexist in a super elongation complex (SEC) enriched with transcription elongation factors (Meyer et al., 2009; Smith et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to Meyer et al., 2009 and Smith et al., 2011.

claim: The MLL fusion event converts MLL into a potent transcriptional activator often giving rise to aggressive hematological malignancies.
source: The resulting fusion event converts MLL into a potent transcriptional activator often giving rise to aggressive hematological malignancies (Mueller et al., 2009; Slany, 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to Mueller et al., 2009 and Slany, 2009.

claim: The overall prognosis for pediatric and adult patients with confirmed MLL-fusion leukemia remains extremely poor.
source: The overall prognosis for pediatric and adult patients with confirmed MLL-fusion leukemia remains extremely poor and necessitates the development of new methodologies and therapeutic agents to improve survival outcomes (Slany, 2009; Tamai and Inokuchi, 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to Slany, 2009 and Tamai and Inokuchi, 2010.

claim: BET proteins are transcriptional regulators that epigenetically control the expression of genes involved in cell cycle, growth and inflammation.
source: Bromodomain and extra terminal (BET) proteins are transcriptional regulators that epigenetically control the expression of genes involved in cell cycle, growth and inflammation (Darnell, 2002; Wu and Chiang, 2007; LeRoy et al., 2008; Dey et al., 2009; Nicodeme et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to multiple sources.

claim: BETs provide potential therapeutic targets for modulating gene expression programs associated with various human diseases.
source: BETs therefore provide potential therapeutic targets for modulating gene expression programs associated with various human diseases.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as an inference from the previous statement about BET protein function.

claim: Dawson and colleagues identified novel interactions between BET family members BRD3 and BRD4 with components of the SEC and polymerase-associated factor complexes in MLL fusion cells.
source: Dawson and colleagues identified novel interactions between BET family members bromodomain protein (BRD) 3 and BRD4 with components of the SEC and polymerase-associated factor complexes in MLL fusion cells (Dawson et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to Dawson et al., 2011.

claim: I-BET151 is a BET inhibitor that selectively binds to the bromodomains of BET proteins and prevents their ability to bind acetylated histone residues.
source: For this purpose, Dawson and colleagues developed I-BET151, a BET inhibitor that selectively binds to the bromodomains of BET proteins and prevents their ability to bind acetylated histone residues (Dawson et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to Dawson et al., 2011.

claim: I-BET151 treatment was extremely effective at inhibiting the growth of leukemic cell lines harboring MLL fusions, including MV4;11, RS4;11, MOLM13, and NOMO1 cells, as determined by their low (nanomolar range) IC50 values.
source: I-BET151 treatment was extremely effective at inhibiting the growth of leukemic cell lines harboring MLL fusions, including MV4;11, RS4;11, MOLM13, and NOMO1 cells, as determined by their low (nanomolar range) IC50 values.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a finding from the original study.

claim: The proliferation of cell lines using other oncogenic drivers, including gain-of-function kinase activity, was either resistant (K526) or significantly less sensitive (HEL, HL60, and MEG01 cells) to I-BET151, exhibiting IC50 concentrations in the micromolar range and above.
source: In contrast, the proliferation of cell lines using other oncogenic drivers, including gain-of-function kinase activity, was either resistant (K526) or significantly less sensitive (human erythroleukemic [HEL], HL60, and MEG01 cells) to I-BET151, exhibiting IC50 concentrations in the micromolar range and above.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a finding from the original study.

claim: Substantial growth inhibition with I-BET151 has been observed in acute myeloid leukemia.

evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to Dawson et al., 2014.

claim: The BET inhibitor JQ1 was reported to have a broad growth-suppressive activity, similar to I-BET151, effectively inhibiting leukemic cell lines, such as MV4;11, while K526 cells remained largely resistant.

claim: I-BET151 transcriptionally downregulated BCL-2 expression in the MLL-fusion cell lines MOLM13, MV4;11, and NOMO1, but not in the K526 resistant cell line.
source: In Figure 3D, the authors confirmed the ability of I-BET151 to transcriptionally downregulate BCL-2 expression in the MLL-fusion cell lines MOLM13, MV4;11, and NOMO1, but not in the K526 resistant cell line.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a finding from Figure 3D of the original study.

source: In addition to MLL-fusion cell lines, I-BET151 treatment correlated with enhanced apoptosis and reduced BCL-2 gene transcription in AML patient samples (Dawson et al., 2014).
